theater: 伊比利亞半島南部與東岸

battle.name: 巴西德征服西班牙
battle.theater: 伊比利亞半島南部與東岸
battle.brief: 公元前237年哈米卡率約二萬人登陸伊比利亞，自加的斯向銀礦推進，前228年陣亡、哈斯德魯巴建新迦太基，前218年漢尼拔抽走西班牙兵轉入義大利。卡面的希臘重步兵非迦太基制式裝備，但恩波里恩與馬西利亞的希臘方陣、希臘重步兵雇兵，與巴卡家用密集方陣操典改編伊比利亞步兵，都源於一套方陣。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前237年至前218年迦太基在伊比利亞半島展開的征服戰役，交戰地域自西南角的加的斯沿地中海海岸東推，最後以新迦太基（Qart Hadasht，即今卡塔赫納）為核心建立迦太基西班牙。迦太基一方是共和國體制：決策在百餘人組成的元老院，日常行政由兩名執政官（suffete）主持，前線則授予統帥（stratēgos autokrator）近乎不受節制的軍權，本役的指揮權實際集中於巴卡家族的父子與婿手中。陸軍以僱傭兵為主體，包括迦太基與利比亞重裝步兵、伊比利亞與努米底亞騎兵、巴利阿里擲索兵，並長期僱用希臘重步兵；海軍是腓尼基式寬身戰船與大型運輸船，負責護送登陸部隊、封鎖港口與維持補給。羅馬當時並未直接參戰，但派特使觀察，並於公元前226年與哈斯德魯巴訂立埃布羅河條約，承認迦太基在河以南的勢力，藉此羈縻迦太基、分化當地部族。希臘殖民地恩波里恩與羅德屬迦太基一方，母邦馬西利亞則與羅馬結盟，三城各自按城邦制度徵召重步兵民兵並僱傭希臘雇兵。對方是伊比利亞各部族與塞爾特伊比利亞人的聯軍，由部族首領各自率領，沒有統一指揮系統。
countriesEn: This campaign was the Carthaginian conquest of the Iberian Peninsula, fought from 237 to 218 BC. The theatre of operations ran from Gades on the south-western corner along the Mediterranean shore and ended centred on Qart Hadasht, the New Carthage of modern Cartagena, which became the capital of Carthaginian Spain. The Carthaginian side was a republic: policy was debated in a council of more than a hundred elders, day-to-day government was conducted by two suffetes, and the field army was entrusted to a stratēgos autokrator whose command was in practice unchecked; in this campaign that command in fact belonged to the Barcid family, the father, his son-in-law and his son. The army was mercenary in its core, made up of Carthaginian and Libyan heavy infantry, Iberian and Numidian cavalry and Balearic slingers, with Greek hoplites employed for long periods, while a navy of Punic-style broad-beamed warships and large transports carried the troops ashore, blockaded harbours and kept the supply line open. Rome did not yet fight in Iberia, but it sent envoys to watch, and in 226 BC concluded the Ebro treaty with Hasdrubal, recognising Carthaginian power south of the river and thereby tying Carthage down while setting the local tribes against it. The Greek colonies of Emporion and Rhode stood with Carthage, their mother city Massalia was allied with Rome, and each of the three maintained hoplite militias on the civic model and hired Greek mercenary hoplites. On the other side stood an alliance of Iberian tribes and Celtiberians, each contingent led by its own chief, with no unified command structure.
people: 巴卡家族的哈米卡是這場征服的開創者。公元前241年第一次布匿戰爭失利、西西里淪陷後，他鎮壓了傭兵起義，看出迦太基失去地中海腹地後必須另建收入與兵源基地，遂於前237年率約二萬人渡海登陸加的斯。渡海之前他任命女婿哈斯德魯巴為海軍統帥，並讓長子漢尼拔在巴爾·哈蒙祭壇前立誓永不與羅馬修好；漢尼拔隨之在西班牙停留十六年，參與其父與其姊丈的全部經營。前228年前後，哈米卡在奧雷塔尼國境內強渡一條河流時，遭部族首領伊斯托拉提奧斯與印多爾特斯設伏，全軍潰敗，哈米卡陣亡。此後由哈斯德魯巴接掌，他改以聯姻、贖金與外交拉攏部族，前227年興建新迦太基，前221年在市集被一名塞爾特伊比利亞人刺殺。漢尼拔隨即接任，清理異己、整編軍隊，前219年包圍薩貢圖，前218年越過庇里牛斯山轉入義大利。西班牙方面值得記錄的對手，還有奧雷塔尼之王奧里索斯與南部的圖爾德塔尼人；希臘方面，恩波里恩與馬西利亞的城邦軍以及羅馬執政官西比阿兄弟的軍隊先後捲入西班牙戰線。
peopleEn: Hamilcar of the Barcid family was the founder of this conquest. After Carthage lost Sicily in the First Punic War, which ended in 241 BC, and after he had suppressed the Mercenary War, he understood that with its central Mediterranean base gone the city needed new sources of revenue and of soldiers, and in 237 BC he crossed the sea with perhaps twenty thousand men and landed at Gades. Before sailing he appointed his son-in-law Hasdrubal the Fair as commander of the fleet, and made his elder son Hannibal swear on the altar of Baal Hammon never to befriend Rome; Hannibal accordingly stayed in Spain for the next sixteen years, sharing in every measure of his father’s and his brother-in-law’s work. Around 228 BC Hamilcar was ambushed while fording a river inside the territory of the Oretani by the chiefs Istolatios and Indortes; his army was broken and Hamilcar was killed. Hasdrubal the Fair then took over, and switched to marriage alliances, ransoms and diplomacy to win the tribes over; in 227 BC he founded New Carthage, and in 221 BC he was stabbed in the market by a Celtiberian. Hannibal inherited the command, removed rivals, reorganised the army, besieged Saguntum in 219 BC and crossed the Pyrenees into Italy in 218 BC. Notable opponents on the Spanish side were Orissus, king of the Oretani, and the Turdetani of the south; on the Greek side the civic armies of Emporion and Massalia, and then the army of the Roman consuls the Scipios, were drawn into the Iberian war.
kits: 卡面的希臘重步兵是這場戰爭裡最需要交代、卻最容易被誤當成迦太基制式裝備的一項。希臘重步兵並非迦太基部隊，但有三重身份出現在本役的戰場上：其一是恩波里恩、羅德與馬西利亞等希臘城市依城邦制度組成的重步兵方陣；其二是巴卡家族在西班牙僱用的希臘重步兵雇兵；其三是最關鍵的一層，巴卡軍隊把伊比利亞與塞爾特伊比利亞步兵按希臘密集方陣的操典改編，用大矩形盾牌相互遮蔽、長矛平舉推進，這套教法最終成型於坎尼之戰的伊比利亞方陣，可以說是hoplite方陣的伊比利亞化版本。同期伊比利亞人自用的裝備是小圓盾（caetra）、短彎刀（falcata）與投槊，適於散兵游鬥而非密集推進；塞爾特伊比利亞人配長矛與長身直刀，遠射用弓、投擲用石索；巴利阿里人則是全地中海最精確的擲索兵，以鉛彈打到兩百步外。騎兵方面是伊比利亞輕騎與努米底亞輕騎的組合，另配少量重甲衝鋒騎兵與象隊，負責破陣與追擊。攻城裝備包括堆土攻城坡道、撞槌與可移動的攻城塔，前219年包圍薩貢圖時，哈米卡門下曾對城牆堆起土壘；海軍提供封鎖與運輸，銀礦則由專門隊伍開採，銀錠經海路運回迦太基。
kitsEn: The hoplite on the card is the item that most needs explaining in this campaign and the one most easily mistaken for a Carthaginian standard of equipment. Hoplites were not a Carthaginian formation, yet they appear on these battlefields in three guises: first, the hoplite phalanxes organised on the civic model by the Greek cities Emporion, Rhode and Massalia; second, the Greek hoplite mercenaries employed by the Barcid family in Spain; and third, and most importantly, the phalanx drill by which the Barcid army reorganised Iberian and Celtiberian infantry, with large rectangular shields overlapping and spears levelled in an advancing front, a drill that reached its final form in the Iberian phalanx at Cannae, in effect a Hispanised version of the hoplite phalanx. The equipment used natively by the Iberians was the small round shield (caetra), the short curved sword (falcata) and javelins, suited to loose skirmishing rather than to a close-packed advance; the Celtiberians carried long spears and long straight swords, with bows for shooting and stones for throwing; the Balearics were the most accurate slingers in the Mediterranean, hitting with lead pellets at two hundred paces. The cavalry was a combination of light Iberian and light Numidian horsemen, with a small number of heavy shock cavalry and elephants assigned to break formations and pursue. Siege equipment included earthen ramps, battering rams and movable towers, and in the siege of Saguntum in 219 BC the troops under Hamilcar threw up a mound against the city wall; the navy provided blockade and transport, while silver was worked by specialist crews and shipped back to Carthage by sea.
tactics: 巴卡家的戰術是海陸並用、步步設營。前237年的登陸採取由加的斯沿海岸線分段北推的辦法，各據點之間以海運維持聯繫；前226年與羅馬訂立埃布羅河條約，等於用外交承認換取羅馬不干涉，讓前線不必兩面作戰。步兵方面靠希臘重步兵雇兵教練伊比利亞與塞爾特伊比利亞新兵，把散兵改造成盾牆相接的方陣：前排長矛平舉越過肩頭刺擊，後排舉矛覆蓋前方頭頂，行軍時以縱隊攜盾前進，接近敵陣再合成密集橫陣。哈米卡陣亡的關鍵也在戰術層面：他在奧雷塔尼人控制的地區強渡一條河，行軍縱隊被山丘上的敵軍截斷，盾牌相接的縱隊一旦被側擊就失去互遮蔽；塞爾特伊比利亞人善用山地與峽谷伏擊，而迦太基騎兵在狹窄地形無法展開。哈斯德魯巴接掌後改以築城固守與部族聯姻鞏固南線，漢尼拔則把前線經驗反向運用：先以伊比利亞與塞爾特伊比利亞輕兵消耗敵軍，再用方陣與象騎聯合作戰。前218年越嶺時他把全軍收攏在唯一道路上行軍，抵達義大利後在特雷比亞河以兩翼騎兵迂迴合圍，正是這支西班牙養成的多族混編軍隊的首次完整演出。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the Barcids combined sea and land and advanced by measured stages. The landing of 237 BC worked by pushing northward from Gades in stages along the coast, with the chain of bases kept in touch by sea transport; the Ebro treaty of 226 BC with Rome exchanged a diplomatic recognition for Roman non-interference, so that the front did not have to fight on two fronts at once. On the infantry side, Greek hoplite mercenaries trained new Iberian and Celtiberian recruits and turned loose skirmishers into a phalanx with shield wall joined: the front rank levelled its spears over the shoulder to strike, the ranks behind raised their spears to cover the heads of the men in front, the column marched with shields carried and closed into a dense line only on contact. Hamilcar’s death was also a tactical matter: in country held by the Oretani he was pressing a river crossing when the marching column was cut by enemy troops posted on the heights, and a column whose shields had been joined lost its mutual protection the moment it was attacked from the flank; the Celtiberians were adept at ambush in the hills and ravines, and Carthaginian cavalry could not deploy in narrow country. After taking over, Hasdrubal relied on fortified bases and marriage alliances to hold the southern line, and Hannibal turned the experience of the front line the other way, first wearing the enemy down with Iberian and Celtiberian light troops and then combining the phalanx with elephants and cavalry. On the march over the Alps in 218 BC he closed the whole army into a single column on the only road available, and once in Italy he produced the envelopment with cavalry on both wings at the Trebia, the first complete performance of the mixed multi-ethnic force raised in Spain.
data: 可核對的數字多出自波利比烏斯與狄奧多羅斯。按英文維基百科所引霍約斯《精通西方》，本役自公元前237年打到前218年，共十九年；哈米卡渡海時的兵力，狄奧多羅斯記為約二萬人，波利比烏斯則說迦太基連一支足以遠航的船隊都難以籌集，他只能徒步走到直布羅陀海峽再渡海。羅馬在第一次布匿戰爭後附加的賠款為白銀一千二百塔蘭特，等於要迦太基失去發動戰爭的能力。銀礦是這場戰爭的經濟支柱：波利比烏斯記載哈米卡開辦的礦場在前218年間向迦太基運回約三萬八千磅白銀，是當時任何國家運回母邦最多的一次。漢尼拔出發時全軍約步兵二萬、騎兵六千，另有戰象三十七頭；渡嶺後折損慘重，抵達義大利時被記為步兵二萬六千、騎兵八千。漢尼拔前218年把其中約一萬步兵、一千騎兵留給弟弟哈斯德魯巴守西班牙，另有後續由馬果率領的援軍開入。坎尼之戰迦太基方面投入約四萬步兵、一萬騎兵，其中伊比利亞與塞爾特伊比利亞兵佔相當比重。地理上，由加的斯到埃布羅河口的海岸線近八百公里，卡塔赫納到庇里牛斯山約五百公里，縱隊行軍每日推進約十五至二十公里，這些距離說明哈米卡的海軍與沿海岸的貿易站補給線是這場作戰的前提。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked come chiefly from Polybius and Diodorus. Following Hoyos, Mastering the West, as cited in the English Wikipedia, the campaign ran from 237 to 218 BC, nineteen years in all. On the strength of Diodorus, Hamilcar took about twenty thousand men across the sea, while Polybius says Carthage was so exhausted that it could hardly provide a fleet fit for a long passage, and that the army had to walk to the Strait of Gibraltar and cross there. The indemnity the Romans imposed after the First Punic War was twelve hundred talents of silver, intended to cripple Carthage’s capacity for war. The silver mines were the economic foundation of the campaign: Polybius records that the mines opened under Hamilcar shipped back some thirty-eight thousand pounds of silver to Carthage by 218 BC, the largest quantity any country had ever sent home. When Hannibal set out he had about twenty thousand foot, six thousand horse and thirty-seven elephants; after the mountain the army was badly reduced, and on reaching Italy it was reckoned at twenty-six thousand foot and eight thousand horse. In 218 BC Hannibal left about ten thousand foot and a thousand horse of that force to his brother Hasdrubal to hold Spain, and a relief force under Mago was to follow. At Cannae Carthage committed roughly forty thousand foot and ten thousand horse, with Iberians and Celtiberians forming a substantial share. In geography, the coast from Gades to the mouth of the Ebro runs close to eight hundred kilometres, and Cartagena to the Pyrenees is about five hundred; a column on the march advanced some fifteen to twenty kilometres a day. Those distances explain why Hamilcar’s fleet and the chain of trading stations along the coast were a precondition for the whole operation.
cause: 迦太基打這場仗有清楚的經濟與地緣理由。第一次布匿戰爭讓它丟失西西里、失去迦太基城的主要腹地，傭兵起義又耗盡了剩餘的財政與精銳；羅馬乘機奪走薩丁尼亞與科西嘉，強加白銀一千二百塔蘭特的賠款，還自行廢棄了終戰和約。腓尼基人在伊比利亞的據點只剩加的斯、馬萊加、阿卜德拉與塞克斯幾個富裕的濱海城市，肥沃的塔霍斯河以南卻有成熟的農業、成片的銀礦和築有城牆的聚落，都不在迦太基的實際控制之下。哈米卡企圖在西西里之外另建一個更強的迦太基帝國，把西班牙變成收入與兵源的來源地。當地部族並不是可以輕易吞併的整體：奧雷塔尼、奧爾卡德斯、伊萊蓋特等部族各有首領與地盤，一旦感到迦太基的稅收與徵召壓力就會聯合反抗，於是這場遠征從一場進攻變成十九年的消耗戰。
causeEn: Carthage had clear economic and strategic reasons for fighting this war. The First Punic War had cost it Sicily and the hinterland on which the city itself depended, while the Mercenary War had drained what remained of its treasury and its best troops; Rome seized Sardinia and Corsica, imposed an indemnity of twelve hundred talents of silver, and then unilaterally voided the peace treaty that had ended the war. The Phoenician holdings in Iberia amounted to no more than a few wealthy coastal cities, Gades, Malaca, Abdera and Sexi, whereas the well-watered country south of the Tagus had mature agriculture, extensive silver mines and fortified settlements, none of them under Carthaginian control. Hamilcar meant to build a second and stronger Carthaginian empire outside Sicily and turn Spain into a source of revenue and of soldiers. The tribes of the country could not be swallowed in one gulp: the Oretani, the Olcades, the Ilergetes and the rest each had their own leaders and their own ground, and as soon as they felt the pressure of Carthaginian taxation and recruitment they combined against the invaders. What began as an advance therefore turned into a war of attrition lasting nineteen years.
impact: 這場征服的直接後果是迦太基西班牙的出現：一個由迦太基人、腓尼基裔商人、伊比利亞與塞爾特伊比利亞雇兵組成的混合體，在卡塔赫納設都、以銀礦供應、以方陣作戰，統治了半島大部分地區達數十年。西班牙的銀與人力決定了第二次布匿戰爭的走向，漢尼拔在義大利能以數萬伊比利亞與塞爾特伊比利亞步兵作戰，用的是在西班牙練成的馬其頓式密集方陣，這個方陣在坎尼一度把羅馬軍團逼入絕境，也迫使羅馬放棄在意大利以外求勝、轉而以海路繞過迦太基的補給線。反方向的影響同樣深遠：羅馬藉埃布羅河條約與西班牙結盟，前218年出兵、逐步把伊比利亞變成自己的勢力範圍，前206年伊利帕一役拔除哈米卡留下的本營後，整個半島逐步落入共和國之手，前197年羅馬劃分近西班牙與遠西班牙兩個行省，開啟了長達數世紀的西班牙羅馬化；西班牙的富銀、銅、鐵礦後來成為帝國財政的支柱之一，而巴卡家用希臘方陣操典改造伊比利亞步兵的做法，也隨着希臘世界本身的衰微而淡出。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the conquest was the creation of Carthaginian Spain: a mixed body of Carthaginians, Phoenician-descended traders and Iberian and Celtiberian mercenaries, with its capital at Cartagena, supplied by the silver mines, fighting in phalanx, and ruling the greater part of the peninsula for decades. Spain’s silver and manpower decided the course of the Second Punic War. Hannibal could bring tens of thousands of Iberian and Celtiberian infantry to Italy because they had been trained in Spain, and the Macedonian-style dense phalanx they used put the Roman legions in serious danger at Cannae, forcing Rome to abandon the idea of winning in Italy itself and to go around the Carthaginian supply line by sea. The effects running the other way were just as deep: Rome used the Ebro treaty to ally itself with the Spanish tribes, sent armies in 218 BC and turned Iberia progressively into its own sphere, and after Ilipa in 206 BC had removed the base that Hamilcar had left behind, the whole peninsula passed by degrees into the hands of the Republic, which in 197 BC divided it into the provinces of Nearer and Further Spain and began a Romanisation of the peninsula that lasted for centuries. The rich silver, copper and iron of Spain later became one of the pillars of imperial finance, while the practice of remaking Iberian infantry in the Greek phalanx drill faded away as the Greek world itself declined.
result: 按戰爭本身的結局，公元前237年至前218年的巴西德征服西班牙以迦太基的全面勝利告終：伊比利亞與塞爾特伊比利亞聯軍沒有在任何一場會戰中打垮巴卡家的軍隊，哈米卡陣亡、哈斯德魯巴被刺殺兩次斷層反而讓迦太基在南部換上更有效率的統治者，前218年漢尼拔帶著從西班牙抽出的主力越過庇里牛斯山，主動把戰場搬到義大利，等於承認西班牙已可不加防守。征服的終結則由另一條線完成：前206年西比阿在伊利帕打敗哈斯德魯巴與馬果，前201年札瑪之戰後迦太基依約放棄西班牙的一切屬地，前197年羅馬設行省接管，前146年第三次布匿戰爭後迦太基本身被摧毀。整體看，巴西德家族用十九年建立的西班牙帝國存在不到半個世紀就歸零，但它在西班牙留下的迦太基城市、礦場、方陣軍制與埃布羅河這條分界線，長久決定了這個半島之後兩千年的走向。
resultEn: As far as the war itself is concerned, the Barcid conquest of Spain from 237 to 218 BC ended in a complete Carthaginian victory: the allied Iberians and Celtiberians never broke a Barcid army in any pitched battle, and the two ruptures in the leadership, the death of Hamilcar and the assassination of Hasdrubal, actually installed more efficient rulers in the south. In 218 BC Hannibal carried the main body drawn from Spain over the Pyrenees and deliberately moved the theatre of war to Italy, which amounted to an admission that Spain no longer needed to be defended. The end of the conquest was completed along a different line: in 206 BC Scipio defeated Hasdrubal and Mago at Ilipa; after Zama in 201 BC Carthage gave up all its Spanish possessions by the terms of the peace; Rome organised the provinces in 197 BC; and in 146 BC the Third Punic War destroyed Carthage itself. On the whole, the Spanish empire built by the Barcid family in nineteen years was reduced to nothing in less than half a century, but the Carthaginian cities, the mines, the phalanx service and the line of the Ebro that it left in Spain long determined the course of the peninsula over the two thousand years that followed.
